facts.text: Automotive simulation advocates in the dense-learning line of work argue that simulation can carry most of the statistical burden, whereas sim-to-real researchers and mining practitioners, including Mining3 and EMESRT, stress field verification and site-specific baselines.
facts.quote: Automotive simulation advocates (the dense-learning line of work) argue that simulation can carry most of the statistical burden; sim-to-real researchers and mining practitioners (Mining3, EMESRT) stress field verification and site-specific baselines.

facts.text: One school of simulation validation tries to reproduce physical sensor observations at high fidelity, whereas another emphasises statistically meaningful scenarios and validates the real sensor through replay and track testing. Current evidence does not establish a universally superior strategy.
facts.quote: One school tries to reproduce physical sensor observations at high fidelity; another emphasises statistically meaningful scenarios and validates the real sensor through replay and track testing. Current evidence does not establish a universally superior strategy.

facts.text: Industry patents and articles present shadow mode as a validation method, whereas academic work treats shadow mode as open-loop evidence with limited ability to prove closed-loop safety. Shadow mode is strong for some safety claims and irrelevant to others.
facts.quote: Industry patents and articles present it as a validation method; academic work treats it as open-loop evidence with limited ability to prove closed-loop safety. It is strong for some safety claims and irrelevant to others.

facts.text: One view keeps machine learning out of the safety function and uses certified deterministic sensors under IEC 61496 and IEC TS 62998, whereas the opposing view accepts machine learning under ISO/PAS 8800-style assurance.
facts.quote: One view keeps ML out of the safety function and uses certified deterministic sensors (IEC 61496, IEC TS 62998); the other accepts ML under ISO/PAS 8800-style assurance.

facts.text: Using a small operating envelope for staged release gives faster real evidence, whereas customers may regard a heavily constrained function as insufficient. No technical principle settles this commercial trade-off.
facts.quote: A small operating envelope gives faster real evidence; customers may regard a heavily constrained function as insufficient. No technical principle settles that commercial trade-off.

facts.text: In the debate over sufficient rare-event evidence, pure exposure counting is demonstrably inefficient, whereas accelerated statistics depend on distributional assumptions. The disagreement concerns how much confidence to place in the exposure model used to decide which rare events matter.
facts.quote: Pure exposure counting is demonstrably inefficient, while accelerated statistics depend on distributional assumptions; the debate is how much confidence to place in the exposure model used to decide which rare events matter.
